h1: The Green Park Grand Yasothon — The Largest, Most Modern Hotel in the Heart of Yasothon
intro: If you want a hotel in Yasothon with a swimming pool, a gym and a real choice of room types all in one place, The Green Park Grand is the name locals rate number one · A 4-star hotel on Wareerachadet Road in the middle of town, with over 100 rooms, gleaming spotless floors, a restaurant and a Japanese restaurant, and parking for a hundred cars · Rooms start from about THB 650/night for a Standard old-building room, up to VIP rooms and suites in the low thousands.

body.html: The Green Park Grand sits at 209/12 Wareerachadet Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon — right in the heart of town, near the government offices, the business district and the market, so getting around is easy · In a province where hotel choices are thin, this is the first pick for people here on official business, for a seminar, or breaking a journey, because it combines a central location with more facilities than anywhere else in Yasothon.

The hotel spans several buildings with over 100 rooms in a range of types — Standard old-building rooms, VIP rooms, family rooms and suites · The thing guests mention most is cleanliness — many reviews describe gleaming tiled floors and rooms so well kept you barely find dust · Rooms are spacious and well-lit, with air conditioning, TV, a fridge and hot water · To be straight about it, some old-building rooms are fairly plain and showing their age, but the cleanliness and room size more than make up for it.
"Spotlessly clean room, gleaming floors, bigger than I expected for the price — easily the best hotel in Yasothon."

What sets The Green Park Grand apart from other places in the province is its large indoor swimming pool, gym and in-house Japanese restaurant · The pool is covered, so you can swim in any weather — a spot families with kids appreciate · There are big banquet and meeting rooms too, making it the go-to for weddings, seminars and functions in the province.

Another thing self-drivers love is the large car park for around 100 vehicles — no circling for a space like at the smaller hotels in town · Staff earn praise for service, attentive and willing, even if some speak only basic English · Foreign visitors passing through Yasothon may want a translation app on hand, but overall it's not a problem.

The honest caveats — the mattresses are fairly hard, a complaint that recurs across reviews, so if you like a soft bed you may want to ask for an extra topper · Opinions on breakfast are split, with some calling it tasty and generous and others ordinary compared to local coffee shops · And taps or shower hoses in some rooms are aging and can leak a little — flag it at the front desk and they'll move you.

In short, The Green Park Grand suits anyone who wants a full-facility hotel in central Yasothon at an accessible price · An overall score of about 8.7 from real reviews across platforms, and the #1 ranking for accommodation in Yasothon on TripAdvisor, reflect exactly that — big, clean, and the most complete set of facilities in the province · Look past the hard mattresses and the dated feel of some rooms, and most guests come away happy.

tips.title: Ask for a VIP or newer-building room
tips.body: VIP rooms are larger and feel newer than the Standard old-building rooms. If budget allows it's worth it, especially if you dislike a hard mattress.

tips.title: Use the indoor pool
tips.body: The pool is covered, so you can swim all day rain or shine — great for kids. Check opening hours at the front desk.

tips.title: Try the in-house Japanese restaurant
tips.body: The hotel has its own Japanese restaurant — a dinner option that's hard to find in Yasothon. Worth a try.

tips.title: Plan around the Rocket Festival
tips.body: If you visit in May, Yasothon's famous Bun Bang Fai Rocket Festival fills the town — book months ahead, as rooms sell out fast.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Green Park Grand Yasothon

faq.q: Where is The Green Park Grand in Yasothon?
faq.a: It's at 209/12 Wareerachadet Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon, right in the heart of town · Near the government offices, the market and Rim Chi Park (~1 km) · About 5 minutes' drive to the Ban Singha Tha old town and ~15 minutes to Phra That Kong Khao Noi.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from about THB 650/night for a Standard old-building room · VIP rooms run around THB 1,200 and family/connecting rooms around THB 1,700 · Prices vary by season and package, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is there a swimming pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes · The hotel has a large indoor swimming pool and a gym, which are rare among Yasothon hotels · It also has Thai and Japanese restaurants, banquet rooms, and a large car park for around 100 cars.

faq.q: What are the beds and rooms like?
faq.a: Rooms are praised for their cleanliness, gleaming tiled floors and spaciousness · However, many reviews note the mattresses are fairly hard, so if you like a soft bed you may want an extra topper · Some old-building rooms are plain and aging — consider a VIP room or a newer building.
Opinions on breakfast are split — some find it tasty and generous, others ordinary compared to local coffee shops · Some packages include breakfast, so check when you book.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone wanting a full-facility hotel in central Yasothon at an accessible price · Travelers here on business or for a seminar, families wanting a pool, or self-drivers needing ample parking · It's the most complete and modern hotel in the province.
